claims.text: Incorporating graphene nanoplatelets into a high-entropy alloy will reduce its coefficient of friction.
Incorporating graphene nanoplatelets into a high-entropy alloy will reduce its wear rate.
The untreated high-entropy alloy exhibits relatively high friction under dynamic sliding conditions.
The untreated high-entropy alloy exhibits relatively high wear under dynamic sliding conditions.
Graphene nanoplatelets can be introduced by either surface treatment or incorporation during alloy processing.
The introduced graphene nanoplatelets will be available at the alloy surface and grain boundaries.
Graphene nanoplatelets align under shear at the contact interface.
Shear alignment of the nanoplatelets produces a stable, continuous graphene-based tribolayer.
The aligned graphene forms a low-shear-strength film.
The graphene-based film reduces asperity contact and direct metal-to-metal contact.
Reduced asperity and metal-to-metal contact lowers friction and mitigates wear.
Graphene's thermal stability enables the tribological benefit to persist from room temperature to approximately 600°C.
The graphene-treated alloy will reduce both friction coefficient and wear rate by approximately 30% or more relative to the untreated alloy.
The beneficial effect should persist under moderate mechanical loads and at temperatures up to approximately 600°C.
Nonuniform graphene coverage or poor dispersion may degrade tribological performance.
Operating conditions that cause rapid graphene oxidation or degradation may degrade tribological performance.
Multiple studies support the ability of graphene nanoplatelets to form lubricious films.
